entries.clue: Clots ordered catalogues (10)

indicatorNotes.ordered: put in order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone orders catalogues and is called a clot for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clots' looks like a plural noun (fools), but it is the verb: blood clots, that is, coagulates.
annotation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken into lumps, which is to coagulate.

entries.clue: Regularly clubbish, helpful youngsters (4)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th

annotation.surface: Young people who go clubbing regularly are nonetheless described as helpful.
annotation.walkthrough: Cubs are the junior Scouts, whose motto is to do a good turn, hence 'helpful'.
annotation.definitionFit: Cub Scouts are youngsters known for doing good deeds.

entries.clue: Lie next to some comma butterflies (4)

indicatorNotes.some: only some of the letters of the following words are used

annotation.surface: Something lies beside a group of comma butterflies.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma is a real British butterfly, named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing, so the surface reads naturally.
annotation.definitionFit: Two things that abut lie directly next to each other.

entries.clue: C. Asian beatniks bizarrely getting into action-film staple (11)

indicatorNotes.bizarrely: the letters of BEATNIKS are arranged in a bizarre order

blocks.note: the Uzi submachine gun, a fixture of action films

annotation.surface: Beatniks from Central Asia turn up oddly in an action movie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'C. Asian' is short for Central Asian, and the definition is an adjective, as is UZBEKISTANI.
annotation.definitionFit: Uzbekistan is a Central Asian country, so something Uzbekistani is Central Asian.

entries.clue: Becoming upset: concession and alternative put before old man (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the column upside down, so it reads backwards
indicatorNotes.put before: the first two parts come ahead of the third

blocks.note: a sop is a concession made to placate someone

annotation.surface: Someone grows upset at a compromise offered ahead of their father.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Becoming upset' reads as one phrase about getting cross; split it, and 'Becoming' is the definition while 'upset' tells you to reverse SOPORPA.
annotation.definitionFit: Becoming can mean fitting or suitable, which is what apropos means.

entries.clue: Heartlessly acquiring grasping Romeo's jewelry (7)

indicatorNotes.Heartlessly: remove the heart, the middle letter
indicatorNotes.grasping: the shortened word holds R inside it

blocks.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet, placed inside EAR…ING

annotation.surface: A cold-hearted person gets their hands on Romeo's jewels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Acquiring' has to be swapped for EARNING before the heart comes out; losing the middle of 'acquiring' itself leads nowhere.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an earring is one kind of jewelry, and the singular answer fits the mass noun as one item of it.

entries.clue: Dairy product moulded, recalled (4)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the word runs backwards

annotation.surface: A moulded dairy product has been recalled from the shops.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheese really is moulded and really is recalled, which is why 'moulded' passes as a description of the product rather than the word to reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: cheese is made from milk, and the Dutch round with a red wax rind is one example.

entries.clue: Ignored (like some consumer goods after Christmas) (10)

annotation.definition2: like some consumer goods after Christmas

blocks.clueFragment: like some consumer goods after Christmas
blocks.note: the post-Christmas sales, where prices are cut

annotation.surface: Something is ignored, rather like goods left over after the Christmas rush.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is the January sales: goods are discounted, sold at reduced prices.
annotation.definitionFit: To discount an idea is to disregard it; discounted goods are marked down.

entries.clue: Everyman's enjoyment? Don't worry about it (2,8)

blocks.note: the setter's own delight, spoken in the first person
the polite brush-off to someone thanking you

annotation.surface: The setter enjoys the work and waves away the solver's thanks.
annotation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so from his own mouth his enjoyment is MY PLEASURE; the question mark flags that self-reference.
annotation.definitionFit: 'My pleasure' is a polite reply to thanks, meaning think nothing of it.

entries.clue: Fat old queen finally consoles those clearly upset (10)

indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'consoles' is wanted: its last letter

annotation.surface: An overweight former monarch comforts people in visible distress.
annotation.walkthrough: To blubber is to cry noisily, so blubberers are people whose upset is plain to see.
annotation.definitionFit: Blubberers are people weeping openly, clearly upset.

entries.clue: Acronym soliciting alacrity, primarily (using initial letters)? (4)

annotation.definition: Acronym soliciting alacrity, primarily (using initial letters)?

indicatorNotes.primarily: take the prime, or first, letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Acronym Soliciting Alacrity Primarily

annotation.surface: A definition of a hurry-up acronym, with a hint about how it is built.
annotation.walkthrough: The same four words both define the answer and spell it with their initials; the bracket spells out the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: ASAP, 'as soon as possible', is an acronym that asks for speed.

entries.clue: Giving Hitchcock film a miss; it prompts you to jump (8,4)

blocks.note: 'giving … a miss' = skipping; the phrase wraps round its object
completes 'giving … a miss', already counted in SKIPPING

annotation.surface: Someone skips a Hitchcock film because it makes them jump.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jump' suggests being startled by a thriller; it is the literal jumping that a skipping rope makes you do.
annotation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is swung for you to jump over each turn.

entries.clue: Gorge shape formed with river – studied by these? (11)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a hint: gorges and their shapes are what these people study

indicatorNotes.formed with: the letters are formed into a new word, together with R

annotation.surface: A gorge carved by a river is something specialists would study.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a landform, so the answer turns back on it: the people who study gorges and rivers are geographers.
annotation.definitionFit: Geographers study landforms such as gorges shaped by rivers.

entries.clue: Bikram, so Amy mostly contorted with hands on hips (4,6)

indicatorNotes.mostly: use most of the word, dropping its last letter
indicatorNotes.contorted: twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Amy, doing Bikram (hot) yoga, twists herself into a pose with hands on hips.
annotation.walkthrough: Bikram is a style of hot yoga, which is why 'contorted' fits the surface so well.
annotation.definitionFit: Standing arms akimbo means hands on hips, elbows out.

entries.clue: Bets glasses will be filled with last of Cointreau after hours (10)

indicatorNotes.will be filled with: SPECS holds the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.last of: 'last of' Cointreau is the letter that comes last in the word
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' puts LATE later in the line than U, so it follows it

blocks.note: after hours = late, placed after U; ULATE then fills SPEC…S

annotation.surface: Drinking glasses are topped up with the dregs of the Cointreau after closing time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glasses' suggests drinking glasses; they are spectacles. 'Bets' is a verb here, as is SPECULATES.
annotation.definitionFit: To speculate is to take a financial gamble, to bet.

entries.clue: Once again asks for some moments of peace? (7)

annotation.surface: Someone repeats a request for a bit of quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: Read as RE-POSES the word means 'asks again'; read as one word, reposes are rests, spells of calm.
annotation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or tranquillity, so reposes are moments of peace.

entries.clue: Coffee leftovers in the gardens and so on (7)

blocks.note: the spent powder left after brewing
the land around a big house: lawns, gardens, park

annotation.surface: Used coffee is being tipped into the garden.
annotation.walkthrough: Coffee grounds really are spread on gardens as compost, which glues the two meanings into one scene.
annotation.definitionFit: Grounds are both the dregs of coffee and the gardens and land around a building.

entries.clue: Gatherings seen in Instagram, Facebook, &c. (7)

annotation.surface: Party photos turn up on social media.
annotation.walkthrough: A social is an informal party; 'socials' is also current slang for social-media accounts.
annotation.definitionFit: Socials are social gatherings and, informally, social-media platforms.

entries.clue: Stinger's tail's removed: it's a sign (7)

indicatorNotes.tail's removed: the last letter is taken off

blocks.note: an arachnid with a sting in its tail; its name loses its final N

annotation.surface: A creature's sting has been removed, and someone takes it as an omen.
annotation.walkthrough: SCORPION drops its N. A scorpion's tail is where its sting is, so removing the word's tail is doubly apt.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Sign' here is a star sign, and the scorpion is the eighth sign of the zodiac under its Latin name.

entries.clue: Artist showing Royal Marines (instead of Navy) in façade (7)

indicatorNotes.instead of: one set of letters replaces another

blocks.note: a veneer is a surface layer, a façade

annotation.surface: A painter depicts the Royal Marines rather than sailors on a building front.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the N in VENEER for RM and V-E-RM-E-E-R appears.
annotation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch painter of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

entries.clue: Empty-headedness in post (7)

blocks.note: a vacant, thoughtless state of mind

annotation.surface: A vacant person has landed a job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link; the two meanings are vacuity of mind and an unfilled job.
annotation.definitionFit: Vacancy means lack of thought, and also an open position.

entries.clue: Those in prang manage OK, we're told, in series of unpredictable events (12)

indicatorNotes.we're told: we hear it said, so the spelling follows the sound

blocks.note: those in a prang (a minor car crash) are colliders; cope = manage all right

annotation.surface: People in a car crash get by, apparently, amid a run of chaotic events.
annotation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash, so those in it are colliders. Said together, 'colliders cope' sounds like KALEIDOSCOPE.
annotation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope, figuratively, is a constantly shifting pattern or sequence of things.

entries.clue: In short, endless cheese (4)

indicatorNotes.endless: the word loses its end letter

blocks.note: in short = brief, minus its last letter F

annotation.surface: Put briefly, there is cheese without end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In short' looks like a framing phrase for the clue; it is the word to shorten.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: brie is one particular soft French cheese standing in for the general word.

entries.clue: Name of lad that's trapped in rotisserie (4)

indicatorNotes.that's trapped in: the answer is caught inside the next word

annotation.surface: A boy has got stuck in a spit-roasting oven.
annotation.walkthrough: A rotisserie is a rotating spit for roasting meat.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'name of lad' asks for any boy's first name, and Otis, as in Otis Redding, is one.

entries.clue: Small child's great power reported (4)

indicatorNotes.reported: said aloud, so we go by the sound

annotation.surface: A little child is said to have enormous strength.
annotation.walkthrough: A mite is an affectionate word for a tiny child.
annotation.definitionFit: A mite is literally a tiny creature, and by extension an affectionate word for a very small child, as in 'poor little mite'.

entries.clue: Love writes on Greek island – fifth of sonnets moving – don't we know it! (4,6)

annotation.definitionNote: an exclamation standing for something everybody already knows

indicatorNotes.moving: the E shifts position within CRETE

blocks.clueFragment: Greek island – fifth of sonnets moving
blocks.note: CRETE with its E (the fifth letter of sonnEts) moved from the end to the front

annotation.surface: A lover writes poems on a Greek island, and everyone knows about the affair.
annotation.walkthrough: The fifth letter of 'sonnets' is E; it names which letter of CRETE moves, from the back to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: An open secret is something supposedly secret that everyone knows, hence 'don't we know it'.

entries.clue: Topple American in overtime (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the first part goes inside the second

annotation.surface: An American toppled during extra time of a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topple' is a verb here, as in topple a government, and so is OUST.
annotation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove or topple them from power.

entries.clue: ... poser prancing with style in artificial fabrics (10)

indicatorNotes.prancing: leaping about, so the letters move

annotation.surface: A show-off prances about stylishly in synthetic clothes, following on from the clue before.
annotation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue the previous clue's surface; they play no part in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: polyester is a plastic spun into thread, so its cloths are man-made rather than natural.
